editorial.headline: Industrial Machinery Leasing: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers operational leasing of industrial capital equipment without an operator—open nationally to all business scales, but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
For a foreign investor considering a Bali registration, the decisive fact comes first: this activity cannot be registered for PMA in Bali today. That local result sits beside—not inside—the national classification. Nationally, it is listed as open to foreign investment, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA registration for every KBLI assessed Low or Medium-Low risk. For this activity, the OSS risk at the Besar scale is Low or Medium-Low across every scope, so the Bali block applies.

At its core, the activity is operational leasing: renting and leasing industrial machinery and equipment without an option right, and without an operator. The equipment is of the kind generally used as business capital goods. The recorded examples give the category its practical texture: textile machinery; machinery for processing or working metal and wood; printing machinery; electric welding machines; and machine tools. The absence of an operator is central to the stated scope. So is the absence of an option right, which keeps the activity within operational leasing as described in the record.

The registration range is broad: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar businesses are all included. A registrant may therefore fall within any one of the four named scales while carrying the same stated activity: leasing industrial machinery or equipment without an operator, generally for use as capital goods. That national scale availability, however, does not override the location-specific PMA result. The Bali moratorium applies to PMA registration on the basis of the recorded risk treatment, including the Besar-scale assessment across every scope.

Both parts of the picture are true at once. Under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, the national PMA position is open and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. Yet a national ownership ceiling is not a Bali registration clearance. In Bali, the block follows the activity’s risk-class treatment and the moratorium recorded for May 2026; it does not reduce the national foreign-ownership percentage. The clear reading is national openness, but no PMA registration in Bali for this industrial machinery leasing activity.
editorial.pullQuote: A national ownership ceiling is not a Bali registration clearance.
